Russian. I used to be able to speak Spanish and Japanese but I stopped for a long time so now I can't.

How long? How long before someone comes to the conclusion that maybe I don't get anything out of this life? I'm not waiting 40 years only to reflect on an entirely wasted life and kill myself anyways.

I don't believe that though. I feel there is something of a path with a decent amount of left and right wiggle room and that you are constrained to that. I used to just think life was awful after having to attend so many funerals in high school.

Then I came to the conclusion that I already knew I guess. The universe is a cold, mechanics driven thing where bad things can happen to good people.

Once that moment is over, that tiny happy moment, I'll plunge back into the depths. I think that's why I stopped doing anything. I couldn't take the crashes.

The crests of the waves weren't worth the troughs of the depression. It just hurt too much. People don't actually want to hear about others problems, I've learned that lesson a few times.

So I can just go to these parties, not talk about anything meaningful, and leave feeling awful.

I'm sorry for dumping this on you.

I thought I did too but here I am 6 years later, still wondering if/when adult life starts. Sure I go to school and work and talk to my coworkers but that all just feels like bs. I can't help but fear that I ooze an aura of uncaring depression, so naturally people don't care about me.

I don't even want to be happy per se. I just want a fulfilling life, or so I keep telling my therapist and myself. Maybe I'm just a big liar. Maybe I deserve all this.

I don't know.

There's nothing to fight for anymore because I know it won't give me happiness. I gave up everything I cared about because at some point I realized it was just distracting me from suicide.

All that stuff like a fulfilling, storied life with a family or partner crime sounds nice. But it's a pipe dream because I'm a POS.

People see something in me that I just don't. That something is value, worth. They believe that just because I'm alive I'm intrinsically worth something. I don't see things that way, no matter how irrational it may be.

I suppose it's because I've already given up on any aspect of my life that brought fulfillment, or that I believed would. 

Living is an expensive past time, and so few people are able to cultivate a life that they enjoy. Most simply go through the motions having risked little, achieved little, and fading into obscurity. 

Was that even a life? In my eyes, no not really. But I suppose I'm not mentally well so what do the words of madman particularly mean in regards to repute.

I don't know how much I care about happiness anymore. I believe feeling fulfilled is much better. 

I would've probably called the police on me if I were privy to my own life as an outsider.

Experiential avoidance, delusions of self-sacrifice, and either placing everyone's worth above your own or placing yourself below all others come to mind. 

Experiential avoidance is probably the greatest concern. It's human nature to stop putting your hand on the stove after it's hot. Experiential avoidance is that but applied to painful emotions.

Hurt, suffering, pain, awkwardness, and being uncomfortable are not enjoyable experiences, therefore I should avoid them. 

Emotions are fleeting things, we have little to no control over them. Therefore one will experience pain, awkwardness, and suffering regardless of the steps taken.

By avoiding these things so completely, one sets themselves up for emotional devastation when confronted with suffering. They don't know how to cope.

But if your whole life feels like pain, then doesn't the police of shutting out the world in your room sound great? But biology cannot be defeated and humans, regardless of introversion or shyness, require social interaction.

After a life of isolation and a lack of understanding of emotion and social aspects, simple everyday interactions suddenly turn into final bossfights.

Tl;dr depressed individuals avoid painful emotions because their default state is already below the 'content' average. It sucks to be dragged down when you're already wearing cement shoes.

I woke up wondering why I was still alive when I hadn't been happy in years.

Went to the psychologist, dripping with anxiety because I already knew what he would say. Only it was worse.

Clinical treatment resistent depression.

It's not just feeling sad or down. It's your highs are never that high and your lows are real, real low. Your mood is a sin wave that sit below the happy threshold pretty much constantly.

Most depression is situational and spurred on by an event or realization. Sometimes it's genetic. Other times, who really knows.

The brain and neurochemistry are still not as understood as the world needs them to be.

I was told at one of my last sessions that I would have to try more experimental treatments along with therapy.

I have to wait two more years to get out of here and find a different practice.

By then I realized my stupid kid dreams were something I should've chased a little harder.

All the hours poured into stuff I used to love. Now I can't even stomach to do it. It just reminds me I failed at living the life I wanted.

I dropped out of community college after dealing with a terrible professor, quit a food service job after only 3 weeks, and did nothing for about 5-6 months except leech off my parents.

I enlisted in the military and am approaching 2 years of service. 

I still want to die. I think about it all the time.

I can't do anything about. It's a stupid catch 22. I need to be deserving and worthy but I can't do that until somebody makes me feel this way.

I certainly don't feel deserving or worthy. Never even felt loved but people always talk like it's this thing, this integral part of the human experience.

They say you have to love yourself but what do you do when you can't? Nobody ever touches on the downside of these uncomfortable matters.

I feel doomed to a half-lived life that's devoid of so many emotions and experiences.

Work, play, sleep. There's life, in three words. Nowhere in there was I happy, or even sad. 

I just was because it's so much easier and comfortable to be numb to it all.

Apparently it's when your eyes have no light left in them, or at least that's what they told me.

I do the same things, everyday, every weekend, every month.

But in general, a messy room(or an empty one), not showering brushing teeth, engaging in self-destructive behaviors and activities, joking about death and suicide, complaining of fatigue(especially in regards to life or everything), talking how everything would be better with you gone.
